newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BITTER FRENCH TASTE TO MILAN'S CLASH WITH JUVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BITTER FRENCH TASTE TO MILAN'S CLASH WITH JUVE.

text.p: Milan's showdown with Juventus at the Stadio Delle Alpi on Sunday has a bitter French taste -- and it has nothing to do with badly bottled Beaujolais.

Didier Deschamps of France and Juventus was in the Marseille side that defeated Milan in the 1993 European Cup final while his team mate Zinedine Zidane masterminded the Italian champions' shock 3-0 loss at Bordeaux in last season's UEFA Cup.
"An unforgettable evening, perhaps the best match of my career," said Zidane on the eve of his first meeting with Milan since then.
The French international's performance that night went a long way towards convincing Juve to sign him.

After a poor start to the season, in which comparisons with former Juve great Michel Platini started to wear thin, Zidane has claimed a regular place alongside Deschamps in Marcello Lippi's midfield engine room -- where the match with Milan will be won and lost.
In a strange twist of fate, Zidane's fellow Bordeaux hero Cristophe Dugarry will also be at the "Delle Alpi" -- sitting on the Milan subs' bench.
Deschamps, however, may not get to see his former Marseille team mate Marcel Desailly. The Milan midfielder is doubtful after turning his ankle in Tuesday's Italian Cup match with Vicenza.
The significance of what is already one of the biggest dates in the serie A calendar grew on Saturday after top-of-the-table Internazionale managed only a 2-2 draw at home to Fiorentina.
Juventus now lie just three points behind Inter. Milan, a further two points back, meet their city rivals next weekend at the San Siro.
With Milan beaten three times away this season and struggling to recapture the form that has brought them four league titles in five years, Juventus must start favourites.

But the European champions suffered a morale-sapping 3-0 Italian Cup defeat to Inter last Wednesday when Lippi tried out the two defenders who are due to appear against Milan in place of the suspended Ciro Ferrara and Paolo Montero.
"We have to go for the three points," said Milan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez, "it's a tough match but victory is not impossible."
abarez will delay announcing his side until Sunday but hinted that Roberto Baggio would be recalled from the substitutes' bench to start against his old club.

Captain Franco Baresi is certain to play only his second match of the season but warned that he alone could not restore order to a leaky defence that has conceded a goal a match since the start of the season.
"Football is about 11 men," he said. "I can do what I can but I alone cannot make or break Milan."
Wise words if Baresi's previous record in Turin is anything to go by. For all his class and experience, he has won just 17 of 64 matches in the Piedmont capital.
Former Ajax defender Michael Reiziger will make his serie A debut in place of the suspended Christian Panucci.

If, as expected, Reiziger's former Ajax colleague Edgar Davids starts in midfield, it will be the first time Milan have fielded two Dutchman in a match since Marco Van Basten and Frank Rijkaard made their last appearances in that 1993 European Cup final defeat to Marseille in Munich.
